metadata.description: Gaming tax rates by state, formatted for frontend calculator
notes: Rates reflect commercial casino GGR taxes as of late 2024 / early 2025 legislative sessions.
Tribal casino rates are compact-negotiated and vary by tribe; only noted here, not itemized.
For tiered states, an effective_rate_estimate is provided as a blended approximation.
Local taxes listed are the most common; some jurisdictions may differ.
Some states operate state-owned/managed casinos where the state retains revenue rather than taxing a private operator.
Rates verified against state gaming commission websites, AGA State of the States 2025, and state statutes in March 2026.

iGaming (online casino) and sports betting operator tax rates added for states where legal. Sources: Tax Foundation, AGA State of the States 2025, state gaming commission websites (verified March 2026).

October 2026: 28 states re-verified against statutes and regulator reports (entries carry lastVerified and sources). Flat add-ons on top of a schedule are coded as additionalRate; handle-based taxes as handleRate with an assumedHold.

October 2026: 28 states re-verified against statutes and regulator reports (entries carry lastVerified and sources). Flat add-ons on top of a schedule are coded as additionalRate; handle-based taxes as handleRate with an assumedHold.

Nevada.localTaxNotes: No GGR-based county tax. Flat per-device and per-game state and county fees (NRS 463.373-.390), e.g. $250/yr slot excise tax and $10/month county slot fee, are not modeled.
Nevada.description: Graduated monthly license fee on gross revenue (NRS 463.370): 3.5% on the first $50,000 per month, 4.5% on $50,000-$134,000, 6.75% above. Thresholds annualized here ($0.6M, $1.608M); large casinos pay ~6.75%.

sportsBetting.description: 6.75% of sports betting GGR. Tied with Iowa for lowest rate.

New Jersey.localTaxNotes: Atlantic City also receives PILOT payments and per-room/parking fees ($3 room fee, $3 parking fee, $2 room surcharge, $2 tourism fee) and the 9% luxury tax; these are not GGR taxes and are not modeled.
New Jersey.description: 8% gross revenue tax (N.J.S.A. 5:12-144) plus the Investment Alternative Tax, satisfied at 1.25% when invested through CRDA (5:12-144.1; 2.5% if paid as tax). Effective 9.25%.

iGaming.description: 19.75% on internet gaming revenue from July 1, 2025 (P.L.2025, c.66; was 15%) plus the 5% statutory IAT satisfied by a 2.5% CRDA investment. Effective ~22.25%. The 8% casino tax does not apply.

sportsBetting.description: Online sports wagering 19.75% from July 1, 2025 (P.L.2025, c.66; was 13%) plus a 1.25% CRDA tax: ~21%. Retail sports wagering remains 8.5% + 1.25% = 9.75%.

Pennsylvania.localTaxNotes: Host municipalities also receive a flat $10M/yr license operation fee (not a % of revenue; not modeled). Category 4 casinos pay exactly 54% on slots (50% + 4% local). Fully automated electronic table games: 34% + 14% + 2% = 50%.
Pennsylvania.description: Category 1-2 slots: 34% state tax + 2% county local share + 5.5% Economic Development and Tourism Fund + 0.5% supplemental + Race Horse Development Fund (18% x racetrack-casino revenue share, capped at 12%; ~8.7% in 2025). PGCB-reported effective slot rate 50.4% (2025). Table games: 14% state + 2% local = 16%.

iGaming.description: Online slots 52% state + 2% local = 54% (4 Pa.C.S. 13B52); online table games and poker 14% + 2% = 16%.

sportsBetting.description: 34% state + 2% local share on sports wagering revenue (4 Pa.C.S. 13C62-63) = 36%.

Illinois.localTaxNotes: Admission tax $2 per person for licensees with <=1M admissions in 2004, $3 otherwise (230 ILCS 10/12(a)). The Chicago casino has its own combined state/city schedule (230 ILCS 10/13(a-5)(2)): slots 22.5% to 74.7% and tables 15% to 35% by revenue band; use a custom rate for Chicago.
Illinois.description: Graduated wagering tax on AGR (230 ILCS 10/13(a-5)(1)). Electronic gaming: 15%, 22.5%, 27.5%, 32.5%, 37.5%, 45%, 50% at $25M, $50M, $75M, $100M, $150M, $200M. Table games: 15% to $25M, 20% above.

sportsBetting.description: From July 1, 2024 (230 ILCS 45/25-90(d)): 20% of AGR to $30M, 25% $30-50M, 30% $50-100M, 35% $100-200M, 40% above $200M, applied separately to online and in-person revenue. Plus 2% on Cook County wagers and, from July 1, 2025, $0.25 per online wager for the first 20M wagers and $0.50 thereafter (not modeled).

sources: 230 ILCS 10/12, 10/13 and 45/25-90 (FindLaw copies; ilga.gov unreachable at verification)

Indiana.localTaxNotes: The $3 admission tax was replaced by the supplemental wagering tax (HEA 1350, 2017). Casinos with prior-year AGR under $75M use a reduced schedule (2.5% on the first $25M, then 10%, 20%, 30-40%). Racinos (IC 4-35-8-1): 25% to $100M, 30% above, on 88% of revenue.
Indiana.description: Graduated wagering tax on AGR (IC 4-33-13-1.5(a), FY2022+): 10% to $25M, 20%, 25%, 30%, 35%, 40% above $600M. Plus a licensee-specific supplemental wagering tax (IC 4-33-12-1.5; ~2.3-3.5% in 2025, capped at 3.5%), modeled at 3%.

sportsBetting.description: 9.5% of sports betting GGR.

Iowa.localTaxNotes: No rate phase-down was enacted (the 2024 proposal, House Study Bill 719, did not pass). Promotional play is fully excluded from AGR from July 1, 2026 (SF 619). Sports wagering 6.75%.
Iowa.description: Graduated tax on AGR (Iowa Code 99F.11): 5% on the first $1M, 10% on the next $2M, 22% above $3M. Racetrack casinos with table games and prior-year AGR of $100M or more pay 24%.

sportsBetting.description: 6.75% of sports betting GGR. Tied with Nevada for lowest rate.

Michigan.localTaxNotes: Development agreements add payments of 1% for casinos with AGR above $400M (Senate Fiscal Agency, 2025); not modeled. Tribal casinos operate under compacts.
Michigan.description: Detroit commercial casinos: 8.1% state wagering tax (MCL 432.212(1)) + 10.9% city wagering tax (9.9% + 1%) = 19%, plus the municipal services fee of the greater of 1.25% of AGR or $4M (MCL 432.213). Total ~20.25%.

iGaming.description: Tiered 20-28% on adjusted gross receipts. Most major operators in the 28% bracket.

sportsBetting.description: 8.4% of sports betting GGR. Among the lowest rates; promotional deductions allowed.

Mississippi.localTaxNotes: The 3.2% local levy applies in most host jurisdictions (e.g. Biloxi, Gulfport, Tunica, Natchez); a few differ.
Mississippi.description: State tax (Miss. Code 75-76-177) 4% / 6% / 8% and local tax (75-76-195) 0.4% / 0.6% / 0.8% on monthly revenue up to $50K, $50-134K and above (annualized: $0.6M, $1.608M), plus a flat 3.2% local tax under local and private laws in most host jurisdictions. Top combined rate 12%.

sportsBetting.description: 12% of sports betting GGR. Retail only; no statewide online betting.

Missouri.localTaxNotes: 10% of the 21% goes to the home dock city or county. $2 admission fee per person per excursion ($1 state, $1 home dock; RSMo 313.820), not modeled.

sportsBetting.description: 10% of AGR for online and retail sports wagering (Mo. Const. Art. III, 39(g)); promotional-credit deduction capped at 25% of cash receipts.

Ohio.localTaxNotes: The 33% is distributed 51% counties, 34% school districts, 5% host city, 3% Casino Control Commission, 3% Racing Commission, 2% law enforcement training, 2% problem gambling (ORC 5753.03(D)). Racinos (video lottery terminals) are lottery revenue, not modeled here.
Ohio.description: 33% of GGR for commercial casinos. Racinos (VLTs) at racetracks have different structure.

sportsBetting.description: 20% of sports gaming receipts from July 4, 2023 (ORC 5753.021, HB 33; was 10%).

Colorado.localTaxNotes: Revenue distributed to state general fund, local gaming cities, and community colleges. Commission may set rates up to 40% maximum.
Colorado.description: Graduated tax on adjusted gross proceeds: 0.25%-20% across 6 tiers. Amendment 77 (2020) expanded bet limits. Max statutory rate is 40%.

sportsBetting.description: 10% of sports betting GGR. Effective rate ~5.4% due to promotional deductions.

Connecticut.localTaxNotes: Mohegan Sun and Foxwoods pay 25% of slot machine revenue to the state under their tribal-state compacts. No tax on table game revenue.
Connecticut.description: 25% of slot machine revenue under tribal compact (Mohegan Sun, Foxwoods). No payment on table game revenue.

iGaming.description: 18% of iGaming GGR (through May 2026, then increases to 20%). Operated through tribal partnerships.

sportsBetting.description: 13.75% of adjusted sports betting GGR. Operated through tribal partnerships.

Louisiana.localTaxNotes: Caesars New Orleans (land-based): the greater of 18.5% of gross revenue or $65M per year (R.S. 27:241.1), plus fixed payments; use a custom 18.5% rate. Racetrack slots: 18.5% state tax on net proceeds after the 18% owed to horsemen, plus 4% local (~19.2% of net slot proceeds to government; inference).
Louisiana.description: Riverboat casinos: 3.5% license fee + 15% franchise fee + 3% additional = 21.5% of net gaming proceeds (R.S. 27:91).

sportsBetting.description: Online sports wagering 21.5% of net gaming proceeds (R.S. 27:625(B), Act 298 of 2025; was 15%). Retail 10%.

Maryland.localTaxNotes: Non-operator slot shares include the Education Trust Fund (27-43%), 6% purse dedication, 5.5% local impact grants, 1% racetrack renewal, 1% lottery agency and 1.5% small/minority/women-owned business fund. Use a custom rate for a specific facility.
Maryland.description: Slot (VLT) proceeds are split by statute, with facility-specific operator shares. FY2026 non-operator shares: MGM National Harbor 56%, Live! 51%, Horseshoe Baltimore 53%, Hollywood Perryville 58%, Ocean Downs 47%, Rocky Gap 42%; modeled at 53% (the three large facilities). Table games: 20% (15% Education Trust Fund + 5% local).

sportsBetting.description: Mobile sports wagering 20% from July 1, 2025 (licensee retains 80%; 9-1E-12); retail 15%.

Massachusetts.localTaxNotes: Category 1 (resort casino, e.g., Encore Boston Harbor): 25% of GGR. Category 2 (slots-only, e.g., Plainridge Park): 49% of GGR.
Massachusetts.description: Category 1 resort casinos (Encore Boston Harbor, MGM Springfield): 25% of GGR (G.L. c.23K 55(a)). Category 2 slots parlor (Plainridge Park): 40% + 9% Race Horse Development Fund = 49%; use a custom rate.

sportsBetting.description: 20% on online sports betting GGR. 15% on retail.

New York.localTaxNotes: Downstate casinos licensed Dec 15, 2025 at bid rates: Resorts World NYC 56% slots / 30% tables, Hard Rock Metropolitan Park 25% / 10%, Bally's Bronx 30% / 10% (statutory floors 25% / 10%). VLT facilities: education receives 34-50.5% of net win plus 10% to the Lottery.
New York.description: Upstate commercial casinos: 30% on slots/ETGs and 10% on table games, a temporary reduced rate through June 30, 2031 (PML 1351(1)(b)); statutory base slot rates are 37-45% by region.

sportsBetting.description: 51% of online sports betting GGR. 10% for retail. Highest online rate in the US.

West Virginia.localTaxNotes: The licensee retains 46.5% of base and 42% of excess net terminal income; purses, breeders and pension funds receive the remainder (not counted as tax). Limited video lottery (bars): 50% of net terminal income.
West Virginia.description: Racetrack VLTs: government share of net terminal income above the FY2001 base (most current revenue) ~52% (inference from 29-22A-10b: a 10% surcharge of which 58% to the Excess Lottery Revenue Fund, then ~50% state funds + 2% county); ~45% on the base tier. Table games: 35% of AGR (29-22C-26). iGaming 15%; sports 10%.

iGaming.description: 15% of iGaming GGR. Proposals to increase to 25% pending.

sportsBetting.description: 10% of sports betting GGR.

Rhode Island.localTaxNotes: Host towns also receive a share of VLT revenue within the operator/town payments.
Rhode Island.description: State-operated through the RI Lottery at Bally's Lincoln and Bally's Tiverton. VLTs: the state retains the residual after operator, technology-provider and town payments, 60.4% of net terminal income in FY2025. Table games: 15.5% to the state + 1% to the host town.

iGaming.description: iGaming: 61% of slot revenue (42-61.2-5.1) and 15.5% of table game revenue (42-61.2-5.2) to the state.

sportsBetting.description: 51% of sports wagering revenue to the state (42-61.2-5); IGT 32%, host facilities 17%.

Delaware.localTaxNotes: Purses receive 9.6% (thoroughbred) or 11.35% (harness) of VLT proceeds, not counted as tax here.
Delaware.description: State-operated through the Delaware Lottery at three racinos. VLTs: 42.5% of net proceeds returned to the state after equipment costs (29 Del. C. 4815(b)(3)a; 40.5% for agents meeting the 3% capital-investment test). Table games: 15.5% to the state + 4.5% to purses.

iGaming.description: The first $3.75M each year goes to the Lottery Fund; the remainder follows the VLT/table formulas after a 20% vendor fee and admin costs (4815(e)). FY2025 state gross margin ~25.5% of iGaming revenue (inference from the Lottery ACFR).

sportsBetting.description: 50% of sports betting GGR. State-operated through Delaware Lottery.

South Dakota.localTaxNotes: City of Deadwood receives a direct allocation from gaming tax revenue. Lawrence County also receives distributions. Revenue funds historic preservation and the general fund.
South Dakota.description: 9% of adjusted GGR. Deadwood casinos only.

sportsBetting.description: 9% of sports betting GGR. Retail only at Deadwood casinos and tribal locations.

Maine.localTaxNotes: Oxford Casino: ~46% on slot revenue. Bangor (Hollywood Casino): ~39% on slot revenue. Rates differ by facility.
Maine.description: Facility-specific (8 M.R.S. 1036). Hollywood Casino Bangor: 39% of net slot income + 1% of gross for administration, tables 16%. Oxford Casino: 46% of net slot income, tables 16% (use a custom rate). Modeled at Bangor's rates.

sportsBetting.description: 10% of sports betting GGR.

Arkansas.localTaxNotes: Tax revenue distributed to state general revenue, host city/county, and Arkansas Racing Commission.
Arkansas.description: 13% on first $150M of net casino gaming receipts, 20% above $150M (Amendment 100 of 2018).

sportsBetting.description: 13% on first $150M, 20% above. Same as casino gaming tax.

Arizona.localTaxNotes: Tribal gaming only. Revenue sharing under Proposition 202 compacts. Graduated 1-8% depending on class III net win.
Arizona.description: Tribal compacts: graduated revenue sharing 1%-8% of class III gaming device net win. Rates vary by volume.

sportsBetting.description: 10% privilege fee on sports betting GGR. Governor proposed 45% for large operators.

Kansas.localTaxNotes: The 27% (K.S.A. 74-8734(h)) is a state share of not less than 22%, plus 2% to the Problem Gambling and Addictions Grant Fund and 3% to the host city and county. State-owned casinos managed by private operators.
Kansas.description: 27% privilege fee on GGR at four state-owned casinos managed by private operators.

sportsBetting.description: 10% of sports betting GGR.

Virginia.localTaxNotes: Virginia Indian tribe casinos pay additional 1% to Virginia Indigenous Peoples Trust Fund. Host localities receive negotiated payments.
Virginia.description: Graduated tax on adjusted gross receipts: 18% on first $200M, 23% on $200-400M, 30% above $400M per calendar year.

sportsBetting.description: 15% of sports betting adjusted GGR.

Nebraska.localTaxNotes: Initiative Law 2020 No. 431. Distribution (Neb. Rev. Stat. 9-1204): 70% Property Tax Credit Cash Fund, 25% to the county (split with the city inside city limits), 2.5% Compulsive Gamblers Assistance Fund, 2.5% General Fund.
Nebraska.description: 20% of GGR. New market (2020), casinos at licensed horse racetracks.

sportsBetting.description: 20% of sports betting GGR. Retail only.

Alabama.localTaxNotes: No state gaming tax on tribal operations. Voluntary tribal contributions to local communities.
Alabama.description: No commercial casino gaming. Poarch Band of Creek Indians operates 3 tribal casinos under IGRA Class II (no state compact for Class III). Electronic bingo authorized at some locations under disputed state law.

Alaska.description: No commercial or tribal casino gambling. Pull-tab gaming and charity gaming exist but no casino-scale operations.

California.localTaxNotes: Tribal casino revenue-sharing payments go to the Revenue Sharing Trust Fund (RSTF) for non-gaming tribes and the Special Distribution Fund for local governments affected by tribal gaming.
California.description: No commercial casinos. Approximately 70 tribal casinos operate under individual compacts. Revenue-sharing trust fund contributions vary by tribe. Card rooms operate under different rules and are not casino-scale.

Florida.localTaxNotes: Compact payments go to state general revenue; pari-mutuel slot taxes go to the state Educational Enhancement Trust Fund.
Florida.description: Pari-mutuel facilities with slot machines: 34% of slot revenue (Fla. Stat. 551.106, 2026; 35% through 2025). The Seminole Tribe operates the major casinos under the 2021 compact: revenue share on slots 12% to $2B rising to 25% above $3.5B, on tables 15% to $1B rising to 25% above $2B (enter as a custom rate for a tribal property).

sportsBetting.description: Statewide sports betting is offered by the Seminole Tribe (Hard Rock Bet) under the 2021 compact: 13.75% of the Tribe's own net win (10% on pari-mutuel partner brands).

Georgia.description: No commercial or tribal casino gambling. Lottery exists. Multiple legislative attempts to authorize casino gaming have not succeeded as of 2025.

Hawaii.description: No gambling of any kind. Hawaii and Utah are the only two states that prohibit all forms of gambling.

Idaho.localTaxNotes: N/A - Tribal compact payments, not a traditional tax structure.
Idaho.description: No commercial casinos. Tribal casinos operate under compacts. Limited gaming (bingo-style machines). The Coeur d'Alene and Shoshone-Bannock tribes operate facilities.

Kentucky.localTaxNotes: Historical Horse Racing (HHR) machines are legal but taxed at ~1.5% of handle (not GGR). HB 33 proposes commercial casino legalization at 21% GGR tax but has not been enacted. Sports betting: 9.75% retail, 14.25% online.
Kentucky.description: No commercial casino gaming. HHR slot machines taxed at ~1.5% of handle. Sports betting authorized 2023 (HB 551). Casino legislation (HB 33 at 21%) proposed but not enacted.

sportsBetting.description: 14.25% on online sports betting. 9.75% on retail.

Minnesota.localTaxNotes: Tribes make voluntary contributions to local communities but are not required to pay state or local taxes on gaming revenue.
Minnesota.description: No commercial casinos. 18 tribal casinos operated by 11 tribes under compacts. Minnesota tribal compacts do not include revenue-sharing payments to the state.

Montana.localTaxNotes: Local jurisdictions receive portions of the VGT tax. Tribal casinos operate separately under compacts.
Montana.description: No full-scale commercial casinos. Video gambling machines in licensed bars and taverns (up to 20 per location): 15% of gross income, i.e. money played less cash credits paid (MCA 23-5-610).

New Hampshire.description: No commercial casinos. Charitable gaming exists. Multiple casino proposals have been defeated. Sports betting is legal (online only).

sportsBetting.description: 51% of sports betting GGR. State lottery monopoly model.

New Mexico.localTaxNotes: Distributions to the state general fund, municipalities with racetracks, and the horse racing industry.
New Mexico.description: Racetrack casinos: gaming tax of 24.8% of net take (Laws 2023, ch. 122) until July 1, 2027, when it reverts to 26%. Racetracks also pay 20% to purses and 1.2% for jockey insurance (not counted as tax). Tribal casinos operate under compacts with revenue sharing of 3-8.5%.

North Carolina.localTaxNotes: Tribal compact payments to the state and affected local communities.
North Carolina.description: No commercial casinos. The Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians operates Harrah's Cherokee and Harrah's Cherokee Valley River under a tribal-state compact. Catawba Two Kings Casino in Kings Mountain also operates under federal trust land. Revenue-sharing details are compact-specific.

sportsBetting.description: 18% of sports betting GGR.

North Dakota.description: No commercial casinos. Tribal casinos operate under compacts. Charitable gaming and limited electronic pull-tabs exist. No state GGR tax on tribal gaming.

Oklahoma.localTaxNotes: Exclusivity fees are distributed to the state Education Reform Revolving Fund (88%) and the General Revenue Fund (12%). No local tax applies.
Oklahoma.description: No commercial casinos. Over 130 tribal gaming facilities. 2020 renewed compacts establish exclusivity fee rates based on game type.

Oregon.localTaxNotes: Tribal casinos make voluntary contributions to local community funds. Oregon Lottery retains proceeds from its own VLT operations.
Oregon.description: No commercial casinos. Nine tribal casinos operate under compacts. Oregon Lottery operates VLTs at some locations but these are lottery products, not casino gaming. Tribal compacts do not require revenue sharing with the state.

sportsBetting.description: 51% of sports betting GGR. State lottery monopoly model.

South Carolina.description: No commercial or full-scale tribal casino gambling. The Catawba Nation is developing a casino in Kings Mountain, NC (across the border). Video poker was banned in 2000.

Tennessee.description: No commercial or tribal casino gambling. Online sports wagering only, taxed at 1.85% of handle since July 1, 2023.

sportsBetting.description: 1.85% of gross handle (amount wagered) since July 1, 2023, replacing the 20% GGR tax. Converted to a GGR rate with an assumed 9.5% hold (1.85% / 9.5% = 19.5% of GGR); enter a custom rate if the operator's hold differs.

Texas.description: No commercial casinos. The Kickapoo Traditional Tribe operates a small gaming facility. Multiple legislative efforts to legalize casino gaming have failed. The Tigua tribe's casino (Speaking Rock) has been subject to ongoing legal disputes.

Utah.description: No gambling of any kind. Utah Constitution Article VI, Section 27 prohibits gambling. Along with Hawaii, one of two states that ban all forms of gambling.

Vermont.description: No commercial or tribal casino gambling. State lottery exists.

sportsBetting.description: 20% minimum revenue share with the state.

Washington.localTaxNotes: Tribes negotiate local impact mitigation agreements with affected counties/cities.
Washington.description: No commercial casinos. 29 tribes operate casinos under compacts. Washington tribal compacts traditionally do not include state revenue-sharing. Non-tribal card rooms exist but are limited-stakes.

Wisconsin.localTaxNotes: Tribal gaming payments to the state general fund (amounts vary by compact).
Wisconsin.description: No commercial casinos. 11 tribes operate casinos under compacts. Wisconsin compacts require modest revenue-sharing payments to the state.

Wyoming.description: No commercial casinos. The Wind River Reservation (Eastern Shoshone and Northern Arapaho tribes) operates casino gaming under compact. Wyoming did not have a tribal-state compact for traditional gaming until relatively recently.

sportsBetting.description: 10% of sports betting GGR. Proposal to increase to 20% pending.
